title: Kinnikuman: Gyakushuu! Uchuu Kakure Choujin
summary: Toei Manga Matsuri film 4 of 7, released 1985-07-13, 39 minutes — Eiren's industry record (03000001541: 1985/7/13公開 39分 カラー ビスタ 映倫24977, 配給東映, 劇場版第4作) and Toei Animation's own lineup page agree, so the wave-4 brief's 'Movie 3, 1984' is refuted and AniList's stored date needs no repair. The film is an expansion of an UNNUMBERED Kinnikuman one-shot: 「キン肉マン スペシャル編 ロビン・メモ!!の巻」, 4-colour, 8 pages, first printed in the Weekly Shōnen Jump special-edition magazine 『キン肉マン熱闘スペシャル』 dated 1984-08-25 — ELEVEN MONTHS BEFORE the film, so the tie runs manga → film and this is NOT a novelization-shaped case. ja-WP states it from both sides (film article: 原作の短編読み切り『ロビン・メモの巻』を基にして、膨らました作品である, cited to Yudetamago's own 作品解説 in 『お〜い!!マンガだよ〜ん』 pp. 186-187; one-shot list: この読み切りを原作としてストーリーを膨らませ…劇場版アニメ『キン肉マン 逆襲!宇宙かくれ超人』（1985年）が制作された), and the English Kinnikuman Wiki has carried 'It is based on the Kinnikuman special chapter Robin Memo' since its page was created on 2007-10-02 — earlier than ja-WP acquired the claim (absent 2008-01-06, present by 2009-01-29, per the page history), so the two are independent lineages, not a copy. All four of the one-shot's beats are in the film, in order: an evil chojin steals Robin Mask's notebook of the Justice Chojin's weak points and kidnaps Robin himself; the villain lures the Justice Chojin to his own planet; Robin is displayed crucified; the villain attacks each of them at the weak points the memo lists; the united 超人サザンクロス defeats him and Robin is freed. The licensor's own one-paragraph synopsis (Toei's lineup JSON, reprinted verbatim by Eiren, and eiga.com's longer version) is, beat for beat, a synopsis of the one-shot. But 8 pages are stretched over 39 minutes and everything that fills the middle is original: Hydra King plus four Hydra lieutenants and four powered-up revivals of TV/film villains (New Ashuraman, New Sunshine, New Black Hole, New Black Rain) and Ukon Jr. — against the one-shot's single villain Booton — eight one-on-one matches, the inverted punchline (the memo's 'weaknesses' turn out to be the things each chojin loves; in the one-shot they were real past injuries, and the twist was Robin's helmet beam exposing the villain's weak spot), the time bomb on Robin's chest and the closing Kinniku Driver. A substantial source share (the film's whole premise, spine and resolution) beside a substantial original share (the entire antagonist cast and every match) is MIXED under T28 — the fork is flagged for Sean below with the numbers. No TV episode adapts the one-shot (no subtitle anywhere in the 137-row run carries メモ or 弱点), so this film is its sole adaptation.

chapters_adapted.note: the UNNUMBERED one-shot 「キン肉マン スペシャル編 ロビン・メモ!!の巻」 (Robin Memo) — 4色カラー8P, 初出 週刊少年ジャンプ特別編集『キン肉マン熱闘スペシャル』1984年8月25日号 (雑誌コード 29936-8/25), ~11 months before the film. It carries NO mainline number in the original run's printed 1-387 space and NO numbered tankōbon collects it: JC vol 37 (2010), the volume that gathers four other Kinnikuman one-shots (マッスル・リターンズ / キン肉マンVSテリーマン / キン肉マンの結婚式!! / ウォーズマンビギンズ), does not include it. Its only book homes are Yudetamago short-story collections — 『お〜い!!マンガだよ〜ん ゆでたまご短編集1』 (Shueisha, Jump Comics, 1989-05, ISBN 978-4-08-871269-7; NDL Search: 1989.5 / 1989.05.15) and 『マッスル・リターンズ』 (Kadokawa, 1997-07-10, ISBN 978-4-04-713191-0, as 「キン肉マン特別編 ロビン・メモの巻」) — so there is NO book-order position among numbered chapters to report. Its printing falls during the Dream Chojin Tag Arc's serialization (printed ch 209-273; the tankōbon shipping either side of it were JC 17 「死闘のかなた…!! の巻」 1984-09-15 and JC 18 「第4勢力の正体!! の巻」 1984-12-15). SIGNIFICANT, not a sliver: all four of its beats carry the film (theft of the memo + Robin's kidnapping → the summons to the villain's planet → Robin crucified → the weak-point assault → the united 超人サザンクロス and the rescue), and the licensor's own synopsis restates exactly those beats. Weight caveat: 8 pages against 39 minutes — at the TV series' own adaptation density (~2 chapters ≈ 30-40 pages per 22-minute episode) a straight rendering would be ~5 minutes, ~13% of the runtime; as a frame it governs the opening movement and the finish while the whole middle (the Hydra roster and eight matches) is original. NEW, never a duplicate: no TV episode in the 137-row run adapts this one-shot, so the film is its sole adaptation.

position.why: The film is set AFTER the Dream Chojin Tag Arc, which our run closes at ep 119. ja-WP (film article): 時系列は夢の超人タッグ編終了後と明言されている; en-WP's List of Kinnikuman films and the Kinnikuman Wiki's Movie 4 page: 'It is set after the Dream Choujin Tag Arc'; and the Wiki's Anime Timeline page ('the intended viewing order of the Kinnikuman anime') lists Dream Chojin Tag Arc (eps 87-119) → Movie 4 → Movie 5 → Psycho Chojin Arc (eps 120-124). The arc's end is ep 119, 1985-12-29 (ja-WP's arc header 夢の超人タッグ編 = 第87話-第119話, whose closing segments are 「前方後円墳に鍵をかけろの巻」/「光り輝くトロフィー! の巻」; the fandom arc infobox prints chapter=209-273, anime=87-119, matching our stored ep 119 → END ch 273). Row identity checked: every date in the context grid (96 = 6/9, 99 = 6/30, 100 = 7/7, 101 = 7/14, 103 = 7/28, 1985) matches ja-WP's 各話リスト row for row, so ja-WP's 第119話 is our ep 119. The stored 100.5 is only the air-date slot (the film opened 1985-07-13, between eps 100 and 101) and is a story-order impossibility: the film's opponents include New Ashuraman — ja-WP's own footnote says the film treats Ashuraman, who reforms in the manga and in the TV series (that is ep 114 「アシュラマンの友情の巻」, still nine weeks away at the air-date slot), as having been defeated and revived into a villain again — New Sunshine is the same case, and Geronimo fights actively here, which en-WP says he does not do until this film (he is in a vegetative state as the Tag arc opens). Caveat in the note below: ja-WP's 明言されている carries no citation and the English wikis said 'after the Golden Mask Arc' until some point between 2013-08 and 2016-08, so the English is a downstream correction on THIS claim; the independent legs are the internal facts just listed.

flags_for_sean: TASK PREMISE REFUTED (the identity half): the brief calls this 'Movie 3, 1984'. It is film 4 of 7, released 1985-07-13 — Eiren's own record (db.eiren.org/contents/03000001541.html: 1985/7/13公開 39分, 映倫番号 24977, 1985年夏「東映まんがまつり」), Toei Animation's lineup page (1985年7月13日公開), ja-WP (劇場版第4作) and en-WP all agree, and the AniList relations in the context (prequel = Movie 3 Seigi Choujin vs Kodai Choujin, sequel = Movie 5 Haresugata) place it there too. Nothing stored needs repairing: title, kind (movie), 1985-07-13 and 39 min are all correct. The wave-2 triage had it right; only the wave-4 brief's parenthetical is wrong.

THE DIRECTION QUESTION, ANSWERED: the one-shot PRECEDES the film by ~11 months (printed 1984-08-25; film 1985-07-13), so this is a manga → film tie, not the novelization shape the protocol excludes. Nothing suggests the one-shot was commissioned for the film: it ran in a Shueisha Jump special-edition magazine alongside reprints of the two pre-serialization Kinnikuman one-shots, and no source connects it to any film's production. The authorial statement runs the same way (Yudetamago's own 作品解説: この読み切りを原作としてストーリーを膨らませ…劇場版アニメが制作された).

THE T28 FORK — YOURS TO RULE (the ask). I propose MIXED. FOR MIXED: all four of the one-shot's beats are in the film in order, and the licensor's own one-paragraph synopsis (Toei / Eiren / eiga.com) is beat for beat the one-shot's plot summary — this is not a quoted fragment but the whole spine, so it is 'a side story that IS the plot' rather than 'an original plot that quotes a fragment'; beside it sits an equally substantial original share (Hydra King + 4 lieutenants + 4 revived villains + Ukon Jr against the one-shot's single Booton, eight one-on-one matches, an inverted punchline, the time bomb, the Kinniku Driver finish). FOR FILLER + a credit in the note: 8 colour pages against 39 minutes — at the TV series' own density that is ~5 minutes, ~13% of the runtime; the film keeps the premise and two signature images (the crucifix, the Southern Cross) but re-executes everything with a new villain organisation and a new twist, and ja-WP's own word is 原型 ('became the prototype') as much as 基にして. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a timed viewing (39 min; on Prime Video JP / U-NEXT / Hulu JP). I found no scene-timed source, so the share above is a beat count, not a stopwatch — that is the reason this verdict is medium and not high. The chapter IDENTITY is high-confidence.

CHAPTER SHAPE: the adapted unit has NO number and never gets one — start/end are null and the piece is named in the note (the Dai / AoT convention for 番外編・読切). Never a decimal (no '273.5'), and never a volume: no numbered tankōbon collects it, so unlike AoT's Ilse's Notebook there is not even a volume hook. If the ledger needs a display label, 「キン肉マン スペシャル編 ロビン・メモ!!の巻」 (Robin Memo, 1984 one-shot) is the honest one.

POSITION CLUSTER: the Kinnikuman Wiki's Anime Timeline lists Movie 4 then Movie 5 between the Tag arc block (87-119) and the Psycho arc block (120-124), but the Wiki's own Movie 5 page says Movie 5 'is set DURING the Dream Chojin Tag Arc' (air date 1985-12-21) and the triage left it at 117.5. The two wiki pages disagree about Movie 5, not about Movie 4. If Movie 5 stays at 117.5 the timeline page's Movie-4-before-Movie-5 ordering is broken; that is a Movie 5 question, and nothing in it moves Movie 4 off 119.5. If you would rather keep films in RELEASE order across the halo, the alternative for this row is the stored 100.5 — say so and I will not argue the story evidence over a display convention.

SOURCE-LINEAGE LEDGER (checked, because two of these are near-copies): kinnikuman.fandom.com/ja is a ja-Wikipedia mirror for this film and this one-shot (near-verbatim 概要 and the same print ref) — I counted it as ONE lineage with ja-WP and did not cite it. en-WP and the English Kinnikuman Wiki are one lineage with each other (the fandom page was created 2007-10-02 carrying en-WP's exact opening sentence). BUT that English lineage carried 'based on the Kinnikuman special chapter Robin Memo' from 2007-10-02, while ja-WP did not have it on 2008-01-06 and did have it by 2009-01-29 — so on the TIE the English and Japanese are independent. On the POSITION claim the order is reversed (ja-WP 2009/2010 first; the English said 'after the Golden Mask Arc' until between 2013-08 and 2016-08), so treat the English as downstream there.

TRIAGE CORRECTION (an addition, not a repair): the owner triage says 'Toei Animation's lineup site carries only the TV series (全137話), no film pages'. It does have a film page — https://lineup.toei-anim.co.jp/ja/movie/movie_niku_kakure/ — whose text is served from /lineup/archive/json.php?category=movie&id=movie_niku_kakure (the page itself is an empty jQuery shell). Its synopsis is a licensor primary and is one of the load-bearing pieces of evidence here, because it describes the film using only the one-shot's beats. Eiren reprints the same paragraph. Worth carrying to the other Kinnikuman film verdicts in this wave.

ja-WP CITATION DEFECT (does not change the verdict): both ja-WP pages date the source of the authorial statement — Yudetamago's 作品解説 in 『お〜い!!マンガだよ〜ん』 — to 1984年9月15日. That is impossible for a commentary about a 1985 film, and it is wrong: NDL Search returns the book as 1989.5 / 1989.05.15, and ja-WP's own 短編収録 table says 1989年5月1日. So the author's statement is from 1989, four years after the film, not a contemporaneous production note.

MINOR NAMESAKE CAUTION for the file: 『キン肉マン熱闘スペシャル』 appears twice in ja-WP — a 1981-09-30 WSJ 増刊号 (which first printed キン肉フラッシュの巻) and the 1984-08-25 週刊少年ジャンプ特別編集 issue that first printed ロビン・メモ!!の巻 and reprinted the earlier shorts. Only the 1984 issue is this one-shot's 初出; do not let the 1981 title collapse the two.
